ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, a regular hexagon and a regular pentagon are placed in the manner shown, with a common vertex O, and side AB of the hexagon and side DE of the pentagon lying on the same straight line. What is the measure of $\angle BOE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Similarly, we can obtain: $\angle DEO=108^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle OEB=180^\circ-108^\circ=72^\circ$, $\angle OBE=180^\circ-120^\circ=60^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle BOE=180^\circ-72^\circ-60^\circ=\boxed{48^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: Use triangle BOE. From the image, read that A, B, E, D lie on one straight dashed line, with AB a side of the regular hexagon and DE a side of the regular pentagon. Also read that BO is the hexagon side from B to the common vertex O, and EO is the pentagon side from E to the common vertex O. From the text, use that the polygons are regular. Thus each interior angle of the regular hexagon is 120°, so angle ABO = 120°. Since BA and BE are opposite rays on the same line, angle OBE = 180° - 120° = 60°. Each interior angle of the regular pentagon is 108°, so angle DEO = 108°. Since ED and EB are opposite rays on the same line, angle OEB = 180° - 108° = 72°.
